story_text.value:
I wanted to share something that Dan and I have been working on for some time. This is the Public Eye, a project that we began with the intention of making congressional bills and actions by legislators more legible.

The Public Eye currently enables agentic search over the sponsorship and voting records of our representatives in the United States. The bot, John Q. Public, directly cites relevant bills for your questions brings you to the key sections of those bills as you discuss the actions of the delegation or individual representatives for any state in the union.

It's currently scoped to the 119th Congress. The agent has tools for RAG over bill text, member info, and various pieces of metadata about bills to enrich and provide citations for answers.

Election Day is nigh so I hope this can be a useful resource for understanding what your reps have been doing for you. We want to continue iterating and improving on it, so please experiment and provide us with any feedback or issues that you run into!

https://the-public-eye.com

https://github.com/mmargenot

https://github.com/danthompson41

story_text.value:
First I built https://bit.recipes to help my family plan our menu and have a Muse agent build the cart and order it.

But pretty quickly I realized they can really suck at this without a lot of guidance in unintuitive ways. So I built a fake grocery store to grade it.

EvalCart is a set of ~2k grocery items and, after ordering, gives the agent a receipt of its execution. Right now it includes a score and feedback on completeness, budget, taste, waste, efficiency, and a few others. The brands are synthetic so if you're testing explicit rules like "Must buy Lucky Charms", that's a gap.

The leaderboard only has some of my own test runs and baselines so far. If you build shopping agents, run one and tell me what's missing.

You don't need to sign up to use it, only if you want to store a history of runs there.

title.value: Show HN: EvalCart – Evals and leaderboard for agent shoppers

story_text.value:
I vibe coded my favorite time-wasting site to look like my wife’s favorite time-wasting site.

I’ve had a lot of fun discovering old posts with this. It builds a profile (saved in your browser, not sent to the server) and guesses your interests based on how you interact with each post. Then you get a mix of content that’s roughly 20% current and popular posts, 20% exploratory posts far from your interests, and 60% posts you’re predicted to like.

I weirdly started working on this a few hours before karpathy posted HackerTube. Honestly was just going to use it for me, then thought maybe others would get a kick out of it.

title.value: Show HN: HakTok – TikTok for Hacker News

story_text.value:
We had problems with Qwen spending too much time reasoning about tasks instead of doing them. That's why we decided to fine-tune it to use fewer reasoning tokens without losing accuracy.

After a bunch of experiments we ended up with KVARK Sparkle 27B.

On our evaluations it uses 34–67% fewer reasoning tokens while getting +- the same scores as the original qwen.

Model is uploaded to Hugging Face with FP8 and GGUF versions available.

I'd like to see how it performs on other people's tasks. To see where it can do worse than qwen.

title.value: Show HN: Kvark Sparkle 27B – reasoning model trained to think with fewer tokens

story_text.value:
I built this as a modern TUI alternative to existing Signal clients, after using gurk for a short while and feeling that the UX could be improved (it's a perfectly good client though; I just wanted something matched to my specific taste).
It is heavily inspired from opencode-cli, btop and neovim. Implemented in Rust using Ratatui. Supports most features I use everyday, including some modern tricks (images rendered directly in the terminal, voice message transcription using local models, adjacent message bubbles morphing together, etc).
The demo on the landing page is exactly the same as the terminal app, but uses fake scripted conversations and contacts. Hope you find it useful!

title.value: Show HN: Faro, an unofficial Signal client for the terminal
